Definition: (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently
BiblicalUsage: This little word carries two meanings that seem far apart, and both turn on softness. Jacob promises to lead his flocks on softly, David begs his men to deal gently with Absalom, and Isaiah says the waters of Shiloah go softly. But the same root names the mutterers and charmers whose soft incantations Egypt would seek in the day of her judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word warns me that gentleness and sorcery can sound alike, and the difference is not the tone but the master. David's gentleness came from a father's heart, and Egypt's whispering came from idols, and I hold that God knows which soft voice I am listening to.
